{# Social and search metadata. LinkedIn's post inspector, Slack, X and Google all want the same things: an absolute og:image at least 1200x627, an absolute og:url, and a title and description that say what the page is. Everything below is derived from the page and mkdocs.yml, so a page only needs to override `description` (and, rarely, `og_image`) in its front matter. The card is 2400x1260 - twice the 1200x630 that LinkedIn, Slack and X crop to - and is rendered from docs/img/og-card.svg. The file name carries the size so that a change to the artwork is a new URL, which is what makes the crawlers refetch instead of serving their cached copy. #} {% extends "base.html" %} {% block extrahead %} {# The docs are read in two places: published on their own, and framed by the app that serves them. The app has a colour-scheme setting of its own, and the Material palette below follows the OPERATING SYSTEM's preference - so a reader in dark mode got a dark app around a light page. The frame is same-origin, so the app's choice is in localStorage and can be read here. It is written in Material's own form - `__palette` names an entry in this file's palette list - because Material resolves its palette in its own script, after this one: setting the attribute here would be overwritten by the very script that decides the scheme. Standalone, no setting exists and the operating system answers, which is what the published site should do. The app also posts its mode on load and on every change, for the case where the reader switches while the page is open. #} {% set meta = page.meta if page and page.meta else {} %} {% set site = config.site_name %} {% set page_title = page.title if page and page.title else site %} {% set og_title = meta.og_title if meta.og_title else (site if page_title == site else page_title ~ " - " ~ site) %} {% set og_desc = meta.description if meta.description else config.site_description %} {% set og_image = meta.og_image if meta.og_image else 'img/og-card-2400.png' %} {% if not og_image.startswith('http') %} {% set og_image = config.site_url ~ og_image.lstrip('/') %} {% endif %} {% set canonical = page.canonical_url if page and page.canonical_url else config.site_url %} {% if not meta.og_image %} {% endif %} {% endblock %}
